disposition: cinnamon named as a compound source
assessment: The Introduction lists cinnamon as a source of eugenol. The experiment used purified eugenol and assessed interlimb function and beam walking in a toxin model. It gives no cinnamon exposure or rigidity rating.

disposition: clove named as a compound source
assessment: Clove appears as a source of eugenol. The results address paraquat-associated motor performance following purified eugenol. No ground clove or dedicated muscle rigidity comparison was tested.

disposition: isolated constituent and animal motor task
assessment: The study evaluated beam and wire performance after purified eugenol. It did not assess daily OFF time, levodopa response or a culinary clove exposure.

disposition: isolated constituent and timed beam falls
assessment: The toxin model recorded fewer beam-task falls in purified-eugenol groups than under paraquat alone (reported p<.01). Beam falls, purified exposure and rats differ from real-world falls after ground clove in Parkinson disease.

disposition: black pepper flavor analogy and reported uses
assessment: Black pepper is one flavor used to describe allspice. Pain appears among folk uses of Pimenta dioica. The experiment measured essential-oil chemistry and antimicrobial activity.

disposition: cinnamon flavor analogy and traditional use
assessment: The report compares allspice aroma with cinnamon and reports traditional allspice uses that include fatigue. Neither cinnamon administration nor fatigue was measured.

disposition: cinnamon flavor analogy and traditional use
assessment: The text uses cinnamon to describe the flavor of Pimenta dioica and lists previous medicinal claims for allspice. Current experiments did not measure pain or administer cinnamon.

disposition: clove named in flavor and antimicrobial context
assessment: Clove appears as a flavor analogy and in a comparison of antibacterial essential oils. Pain is a reported traditional allspice use. The paper gives no clove and pain comparison.
